title: Decide the record for cloud/sandbox: finish the deletion or amend the epic's claim
description:
Found by the pwp close-out (tick 8vl, attempt 11).

Tick 3r2's GOES list AND the pwp epic's acceptance criteria both state that cloud/sandbox is deleted. The integrated branch still carries it: Dockerfile, entrypoint.sh, worker.sh, common.sh, preflight.sh — a 236K build context.

The worker had a real reason to keep it: internal/sandbox shells into those scripts to warm local worktrees, and internal/sandbox was never in delete scope. But that deviation is recorded ONLY in a comment in embedded.go. No tick note, no finding, nothing in the tracker. The final review's survival checklist never re-checked the epic's acceptance criteria, so the drift went unnoticed and the epic record now asserts a deletion that did not happen.

This is a record-integrity problem first and a cleanup second. Pick one and write it down:
(a) Finish the deletion — move the scripts somewhere internal/sandbox can reach, or into ticfac.
(b) Amend the epic record to state that cloud/sandbox stays and why, so the acceptance criteria stop claiming otherwise.

Separately worth noting for future epics: an acceptance criterion that names a deletion should be re-checked mechanically at close-out, not trusted from the plan.
notes:
2026-09-17 12:38 - DECIDED ON THE TICFAC SIDE (tick 5bp, run epic-9pd, 2026-09-17). This is the answer g69 was written to reach.

Authority: THIS repository owns cloud/sandbox. ticfac vendors it as a pinned copy, recorded in sandbox.pin.json at ref e1146e6da773e2b7d6ad9178faa1fd367466d5b8, verified offline on every ticfac test run and byte-for-byte against this repository at that ref in ticfac's CI.

What that means for an editor here: a consumer follows this tree at a pin, so a change must be adoptable — ticfac bumps the pin deliberately, the way it bumps the contract bundle and the herdr wire vocabulary. It is no longer a copy that can drift silently (ticfac tick 5bp; the drift risk was found by tick e08).

g69's remaining job is to record this on this side so the two trackers cannot hold contradictory decisions about one tree, and to settle the related record gap: the pwp epic's description and tick 3r2's GOES list both still said cloud/sandbox was deleted (see also l49).
acceptance_criteria: Either cloud/sandbox is gone from this repository and internal/sandbox still warms worktrees, or the pwp epic record explicitly states that cloud/sandbox remains and why; in both cases no acceptance criterion claims a deletion that did not happen
